newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock hike expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, LME stock hike expected.

text.p: COMEX copper tumbled by close after a key prop to prices fizzled on Monday, leaving the market to expect an anticipated rise in London red metal stocks Tuesday, traders said.
Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the market sailed uneventfully through the technical tightness in LME December Third Wednesday pricing which takes place on the prior Monday.
"But I was surprised we went down as much. I would have thought it was well anticipated," Hirsch said.
March COMEX went out 2.65 cents weaker at 96.65 cents per pound, traded 99.50 to 96.20 cents. Spot December settled 2.45 cents lower at 100.05 cents.
Traders were now waiting for Tuesday's LME stock report, with a hike of 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes expected. "It will be interesting to see how much of an increase there is in the U.S.," Hirsch added.

LME stocks in the U.S. rose about 7,000 tonnes Friday, with much of the hike due to "truck shuffling" between COMEX and LME warehouses, traders said, leaving overall COMEX-LME stocks in the U.S. largely unchanged.
